title: What the Python SDK returns: result, response and error, and why try/except misses API errors

prose.text: The Python SDK reports API errors in its return value by default, though some calls raise regardless. How its pages are walked is in [[zia.sdk-python.pagination]], and its retry and rate-limit behavior is in [[zia.api.rate-limits]].

prose.label: Errors are values.
prose.text: {{errors-in-third-slot}} {{validation-errors-returned}} {{callers-must-check-error}} Whether a later SDK release will raise instead is open {{gap:raise-proposal}}.

checks.do: Whether the call site unpacks all three values and tests the error value before using the result.
Whether a test double returns a tuple rather than raising, since a raising mock does not match the SDK.
Whether a configuration rejected by the SDK came back as an error value rather than an exception.

errors-in-third-slot.statement: A ZIA list call catches its own exceptions and returns them in the third slot with a None result, instead of raising.

validation-errors-returned.statement: The SDK's own pre-send validation also comes back as an error value: updating the advanced URL filter settings with CIPA compliance and a mutually exclusive setting both true returns a ValueError in the tuple.

quotes: ValueError(f"Invalid configuration: '{key}' cannot be True when 'enable_cipa_compliance' is True"),
Updates the URL and Cloud App Control advanced policy settings

callers-must-check-error.statement: So a try/except around a ZIA SDK call does not catch API errors; the caller has to test the error value of every returned tuple, and a test double has to return tuples rather than raise.
callers-must-check-error.conditions: Holds with the default `raiseException=False` (with True, `check_response_for_error` raises `ZscalerAPIException`), for calls that complete the request path as the ZIA methods read at the pin do; construction errors and the page iterator can still raise.

single-assignment-yields-tuple.statement: Assigning a call to a single name therefore binds the whole tuple, not the list or object, so iterating it yields the result, response and error.
single-assignment-yields-tuple.conditions: Follows directly from the return shape.

result-models-snake-case-attrs.statement: A result model exposes snake_case attributes; its request_format output uses the API's camelCase keys, and as_dict converts those keys to snake_case and leaves out None values. The URL category model reads customCategory into custom_category, and its request_format writes it back as customCategory.
result-models-snake-case-attrs.conditions: Corrected because as_dict, inherited from the base class, returns snake_case keys; the camelCase entry is in request_format. Previously "A result model exposes snake_case attributes but its as_dict output uses the API's camelCase keys: the URL category model reads customCategory into custom_category and writes it back as customCategory."

quotes: self.custom_category = config["customCategory"] if "customCategory" in config else False
# Otherwise it's a simple type (string, int, etc.) else: result[to_snake_case(key)] = val
The keys are in camelCase as expected by the API.

raise-proposal.title: Whether the SDK maintainers will change the SDK to raise on errors
raise-proposal.detail: Unverified legacy statement: An upstream issue (zscaler-sdk-python #297, open at capture) is said to quote the maintainers on every endpoint repeating a catch that returns the exception in the tuple, and to propose raising instead; the issue is not in the vendored tree and the statement that the pattern was carried over from the Go SDK is also unsourced here.
raise-proposal.blocks: Whether to rely on try/except in scripts written against a newer SDK release.
